name: Windows — New Interactive RDP Logon to a Host
description: Alerts the first time a given user account logs on interactively over RDP (logon type 10) to a given host, measured against a rolling 14-day history. RDP is tightly restricted at JCB — only 358 type-10 logons across 75 hosts in 7 days — which makes a previously unseen user/host RDP pair a strong lateral-movement signal rather than background noise. No existing rule covers RDP logon type 10.
author: ScanWave
note:
### Triage
1. Confirm the user/host pair against the expected administrative model: does this person normally administer this server?
2. Recover `source.ip` from the event to establish where the session originated; an RDP session sourced from a workstation subnet into the server estate, or from a server into another server, is the classic RDP-chaining pattern.
3. Review what the account did after logon: process creation (4688), service installs, and share access on the destination.
4. Correlate with `Windows — Potential SharpRDP Behavior` and with FortiGate traffic for RDP crossing network zones.
false_positives: A new administrator or a role change legitimately introducing a new user/host pair.
Helpdesk staff covering an unfamiliar system for the first time.
